entry: Vector differential operator, usually written ∇ and called nabla, used in [[Vector calculus|vector calculus]]. Applied to a function on a one-dimensional domain, it denotes the standard [[Derivative|derivative]] of that function. Applied to a field, it denotes one of three operations: the [[Gradient|gradient]] (steepest slope) of a scalar field, the divergence of a vector field, or the curl (rotation) of a vector field. Del is a convenient notation for these operations, making many equations easier to write and remember. Formally, it is a vector operator whose components are the [[Partial derivative|partial derivative]] operators. The gradient of a scalar field points in the direction of greatest increase, and its magnitude equals the maximum rate of increase at that point.

U.S. state in the Mid-Atlantic and South Atlantic regions. Its name derives from the adjacent Delaware Bay, named after Thomas West, 3rd Baron De La Warr, Virginia's first colonial-era governor. Delaware took part in the [[American Revolution]] and, on December 7, 1787, became the first state to ratify the [[Constitution of the United States]], earning the nickname "The First State." Over half of [[New York Stock Exchange]]-listed corporations and over three-fifths of the Fortune 500 are legally incorporated there.

[[Rapid transit]] system serving [[Delhi]] and the National Capital Region of [[India]]. It has 10 color-coded lines and 271 stations over 374.466 km, and is India's largest and busiest metro system. Construction began in 1998, and the first elevated section opened on December 25, 2002. Operated by the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation, a joint venture of the [[Government of India]] and the Government of Delhi, it was certified by the [[United Nations]] in 2011 as the first metro rail and rail-based system in the world to receive carbon credits. Annual ridership was 235.8 crore (2.35 billion) in 2025.

Late medieval empire based in [[Delhi]], covering much of the Indian subcontinent (1206–1526). The sultanate was established in 1206 in former Ghurid territories. Its history is divided into five periods: Mamluk (1206–1290), Khalji (1290–1320), Tughlaq (1320–1414), Sayyid (1414–1451), and Lodi (1451–1526). Its territory included parts of modern [[India]], [[Pakistan]], [[Bangladesh]], and southern [[Nepal]], and it reached its greatest extent under the Tughlaq dynasty. In 1398 the Central Asian ruler [[Timur]] raided Delhi, and in 1526 [[Babur]] conquered the sultanate, which was succeeded by the Mughal Empire. The period saw the development of the [[Hindustani language]] and Indo-Islamic architecture.

Confederacy of Greek city-states under [[Athens|Athenian]] leadership, founded in 478 BC to continue fighting the Persian Empire after the Greek victory at the Battle of Plataea. Its membership numbered between 150 and 330 states. The league functioned as a dual offensive and defensive alliance of autonomous states, similar to the rival Peloponnesian League led by [[Sparta]]. Its name derives from its meeting place on the island of Delos, where congresses were held in the sanctuary of the Temple of [[Apollo]]. By the mid-fifth century BC, Athens had established dominion over the league, which became known as the Athenian Empire, and its allies had lost much of their autonomy. In 454 BC, [[Pericles]] moved the league's treasury to Athens. The threat the league posed to Spartan hegemony helped prompt the [[Peloponnesian War]] in 431 BC. The league was dissolved at the war's end in 404 BC under Lysander, and Athens partly revived it as the Second Athenian League.

Rapid onset of confusion caused by withdrawal from alcohol. The name is literally "trembling delirium." It typically begins 48–72 hours after the last use of alcohol and lasts 1–8 days. Symptoms include nightmares, confusion, disorientation, heavy sweating, elevated heart rate and blood pressure, and [[Hallucination|hallucinations]]. It can be fatal, especially without treatment, from very high body temperature, seizures, [[Respiratory failure|respiratory failure]], or [[Arrhythmia|cardiac arrhythmias]]. Aggressive treatment with [[Benzodiazepine|benzodiazepines]] improves outcomes.

American technology company based in Round Rock, Texas. [[Michael Dell]] founded it in 1984 as PC's Limited, making [[IBM]] clone computers and pioneering direct sales of cut-price [[Personal computer|personal computers]]. In 2001 it became the largest global PC vendor for the first time. Its products include servers, [[Data storage|data storage]] devices, network switches, [[Software|software]], and [[Printer (computing)|printers]]. In 2015 it acquired EMC Corporation, and it is a subsidiary of Dell Technologies.

Multinational professional services network based in [[London]], one of the Big Four accounting firms along with EY, [[KPMG]], and [[PwC]]. Founded by accountant William Welch Deloitte in London in 1845, it expanded into the United States in 1890. Its services include audit, consulting, financial advisory, risk, [[Tax|tax]], and legal work, with approximately 470,000 employees in over 150 countries. In FY 2024 the network earned revenues of US$67.2 billion in aggregate. A 2017 cyberattack caused a breach of client confidentiality and publicized significant employee information.

Major United States airline headquartered in [[Atlanta]], Georgia, operating nine hubs. [[Hartsfield–Jackson Atlanta International Airport]] is its largest hub by total passengers and departures. Including regional affiliates operating under the Delta Connection brand, it has over 5,400 daily flights to 325 destinations in 52 countries on six continents. One of the oldest still-operating commercial airlines in the United States, it began passenger operations in 1929. At the turn of the 21st century it was a founding member of SkyTeam.

Fixed belief resistant to conflicting evidence. Unlike beliefs based on false or incomplete information, [[Hallucination|hallucinations]], or other misleading perceptions, delusions are not revised when evidence contradicts them. Delusions occur in many physical and mental disorders and are of particular diagnostic importance in psychotic disorders, including [[Schizophrenia|schizophrenia]], paraphrenia, manic episodes of [[Bipolar disorder|bipolar disorder]], and psychotic depression. They are commonly divided into bizarre delusions, which are clearly implausible, and non-bizarre delusions, which are false but technically possible. They can also be classed as mood-congruent, matching a depressive or manic state, or mood-neutral. Common themes include persecutory delusions, delusions of control, and erotomania, the false belief that another person, often a famous figure, is in love with the believer.

[[Twelve Olympians|Olympian]] goddess of the [[Harvest|harvest]] and [[Agriculture|agriculture]] in ancient Greek religion. She presided over [[Crop|crops]], grain, food, and the fertility of the earth, and she was also linked with health, birth, marriage, and the underworld. Her daughter Persephone was abducted by [[Hades]], and Demeter's grief brought famine until [[Zeus]] ordered Hades to return her. Because Persephone had eaten food from the underworld, she divided each year between her mother and Hades, which explains the seasons. Demeter and Persephone were central to the Eleusinian Mysteries, and Romans identified her with Ceres.

American actress and film producer. After joining the soap opera [[General Hospital]] in 1981, she became a member of the Brat Pack, appearing in films such as *St. Elmo's Fire* (1985). Her performance in *Ghost* (1990) made her a star, and by 1995 she had become the world's highest-paid actress. She received $12.5 million to star in *Striptease* (1996). For *The Substance* (2024), she won a Golden Globe and an Academy Award nomination for Best Actress.

British [[Artificial intelligence|artificial intelligence]] researcher and entrepreneur. He is chairman and co-founder of [[Google]] DeepMind and chief scientist of Alphabet, and he is chief executive officer and co-founder of Isomorphic Labs. A child prodigy in [[Chess|chess]], he was earlier a video game AI programmer and designer. In 2024 he and John M. Jumper were jointly awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for AI research on protein structure prediction. He was knighted that year for his work on AI and is a Fellow of the Royal Society.

Artisan-like figure in [[Plato|Platonic]] and Neoplatonic philosophy, responsible for fashioning and maintaining the physical universe. In Plato's *Timaeus* (c. 360 BC), the demiurge is a benevolent creator that fashions the world after eternal Forms and makes lesser gods, who in turn make humanity. Some scholars argue that these lower gods are deities of traditional mythology, such as [[Zeus]] and Hera. [[Gnosticism|Gnostic]] schools also adopted the term, and in Gnostic traditions the demiurge is generally a lesser divinity who governs the material universe.

Liberal political party in the United States, on the center to center-left of the political spectrum. Founded in 1828, it is the world's oldest active political party and the main rival of the [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican Party]]. [[Franklin D. Roosevelt]] won the presidency in 1932 on a strong response to the [[Great Depression]], and his [[New Deal]] built a broad coalition. In 1860 the party split into Northern and Southern factions over slavery, and after [[Bill Clinton]]'s election in 1992 it moved toward centrism. It supports healthcare reform, paid sick leave, paid family leave, and unions, and advocates abortion rights, gun control, and action on [[Climate change|climate change]].

American political party founded in the early 1790s by [[Thomas Jefferson]] and [[James Madison]]. Known at the time as the Republican Party, it championed decentralization, agrarianism, free markets, and separation of church and state. It became dominant after the 1800 elections, when the [[Federalist Party]] collapsed. After the 1824 presidential election, the party split: one faction became the National Republican Party, later part of the [[Whig Party (United States)|Whig Party]], while another backed [[Andrew Jackson]] and became the modern [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic Party]].

Left-wing political philosophy combining political democracy with a socially owned economy. Its emphasis falls on economic democracy, workplace democracy, and workers' self-management. Democratic socialists argue that [[Capitalism|capitalism]] is incompatible with freedom, equality, and solidarity, and most seek a gradual transition to [[Socialism|socialism]]. The movement was popularized by socialists who opposed the one-party state of the [[Soviet Union]], and it is distinguished from [[Social democracy|social democracy]], which leaves many businesses in private ownership.

Pre-Socratic Greek philosopher from Abdera, remembered for formulating an [[Atom|atomic]] theory of the [[Universe|universe]]. He was a [[Polymath|polymath]] and prolific writer who produced nearly 80 treatises on subjects including poetry, harmony, military tactics, and Babylonian theology. None of his original work survives, and he is known mainly through second-hand references, many from [[Aristotle]], who viewed him as an important rival in natural philosophy. Ancient writers called him the "laughing philosopher" for his emphasis on the value of cheerfulness. According to Aristotle, he was born in Abdera on the coast of Thrace, and he spent his inheritance on travels in search of knowledge.

Statistical study of human populations, covering their size, composition (such as ethnic group and age), and change through fertility, mortality, and migration. Formal demography measures these processes, while social demography, or population studies, also analyzes their links to economic, social, institutional, cultural, and biological factors. Educational institutions usually treat it as a field of [[Sociology|sociology]], although independent departments exist. Demographic analysis uses administrative records to produce estimates often considered a reliable standard for judging [[Census|census]] accuracy. In 1662 John Graunt's study of mortality records found that one-third of London's children died before their sixteenth birthday, and mathematicians such as [[Edmond Halley]] developed the life table as the basis for life insurance mathematics.

Evil or malevolent supernatural entity. Belief in demons appears in [[Folklore|folklore]], mythology, religion, occultism, and literature, and probably dates to the [[Paleolithic]] age. In [[Abrahamic religions]], a demon is a harmful spiritual entity that may cause possession and require exorcism. Demons may be considered minions of the [[Devil]], causing sinful thoughts and tempting people to sin. The Greek word daimōn originally had no negative connotation, and in [[Plato]]'s works it describes the divine inspiration of Socrates. In [[Christianity]], morally ambivalent daimōn were replaced by demons as hostile forces of evil. In [[Western esotericism|Western esotericism]], a demon is believed to be a spirit that can be conjured and controlled.

Japanese [[Manga|manga]] series written and illustrated by Koyoharu Gotouge. Serialized in Shueisha's shōnen magazine *Weekly Shōnen Jump* from February 2016 to May 2020, it follows Tanjiro Kamado, who joins the Demon Slayer Corps after his family is slaughtered and his sister Nezuko is turned into a demon. Its [[Anime|anime]] adaptation by Ufotable began in 2019, and its 2020 film *Mugen Train* became the highest-grossing anime and Japanese film of all time. By July 2025 the manga had over 220 million copies in circulation, including digital versions.

Classical Athenian statesman and orator. He learned [[Rhetoric|rhetoric]] by studying earlier great orators and worked as a logographer, writing speeches for private lawsuits. In 354 BC he gave his first public political speeches, and he devoted his most productive years to opposing the expansion of [[Macedonia (ancient kingdom)|Macedon]] under [[Philip II of Macedon]]. After Philip's death he led Athens's uprising against [[Alexander the Great]], which failed. To avoid arrest by an agent of Antipater, he killed himself. The Alexandrian Canon ranked him among the ten greatest Attic orators, and [[Cicero]] called him "the perfect orator."

Highest mountain in [[North America]], in the Alaska Range of interior [[Alaska]]. Its summit is 20,310 feet (6,190 m) above [[Sea level|sea level]], and it is the centerpiece of Denali National Park and Preserve. It is the third most prominent peak on Earth, after [[Mount Everest]] and [[Aconcagua]]. The Koyukon people have called it "Denali" for centuries. In 1896 a gold prospector named it Mount McKinley in support of then presidential candidate [[William McKinley]]. The first verifiable ascent was made on June 7, 1913. The U.S. Department of the Interior changed the federal name to Denali in 2015 and reverted it to Mount McKinley in January 2025.

Chinese statesman and revolutionary, paramount leader of the [[China|People's Republic of China]] from 1978 to 1989. Following [[Mao Zedong]]'s death in 1976, he guided the country into [[Reform and opening up|reform and opening up]], which introduced market incentives, special economic zones, and foreign investment. He is credited as the "architect of modern China." During the [[Cultural Revolution]], he was purged twice by Mao. He negotiated the handovers of Hong Kong and Macau and formulated the principle of "one country, two systems." He was named *Time* Person of the Year in 1978 and 1985. He ordered the 1989 crackdown on the Tiananmen Square protests, which remains a subject of international condemnation.

Mosquito-borne disease caused by any of four dengue virus serotypes. Most infections are asymptomatic or mild, with fever, headache, muscle and joint pains, and a rash appearing 3 to 14 days after infection. In a small proportion of cases the disease becomes severe, with bleeding, [[Blood plasma|blood plasma]] leakage, and dangerously low blood pressure. Infection with one serotype usually gives lifelong immunity to it but only short-term immunity to the others, and a later infection with another serotype raises the risk of severe disease through [[Antibody|antibody]]-dependent enhancement. There is no specific medication, and severe cases require hospitalization for fluids. Partly attributed to [[Climate change|climate change]], the disease is spreading to the [[Iberian Peninsula]] and the southern United States. In 2023 more than 5 million infections were reported, with more than 5,000 dengue-related deaths.
